title: Lacson seeks return of P8.1B cut from DOTr budget for Davao, Cebu projects
summary: Senator Panfilo Lacson on Thursday called for the restoration of the P8.1 billion slashed from the budget of the Department of Transportation (DOTr) that would support two foreign-assisted projects…

blocks.text: Senator Panfilo Lacson on Thursday called for the restoration of the P8.1 billion slashed from the budget of the Department of Transportation (DOTr) that would support two foreign-assisted projects (FAPs) located in Davao City and Cebu province.
This was raised during the Senate plenary deliberations on the proposed P295.797 billion budget of the Department of Transportation (DOTr) and its attached agencies for fiscal year 2027.
In his interpellation, Lacson decried the P5.1 billion budget cut for the Davao Public Transport Modernization Program, as well as another P3 billion for the New Cebu International Container Port.
“Ito ‘yung mga growth-oriented investment na dapat nating i-prioritize instead of the usual…katakot-takot na ayudas,” he said.
(These are the growth-oriented investments that we should prioritize instead of the questionable financial aids.)

“These are, I think, priority, not only because it entails some payment of penalties and commitment fees, but because growth-oriented investment nga ito eh at saka commitment natin ito para hindi tayo makakuha ng loan (these are growth-oriented investments and this is our commitment so we don’t have to seek a loan),” he added.

Senator JV Ejercito, chairman of the Senate finance committee and budget sponsor for DOTr, noted the government already incurred P20 million in commitment fees and penalties due to delays from December 2023 up to June 2026.
Lacson warned that it may cost the government more if these projects do not resume by next year.
“Roughly, it’s about P3 million a year,” Ejercito answered.
Regardless, he acknowledged that these projects should be well funded as they will benefit the country’s economy.

“Anything for infrastructure. You know that’s one of my advocacies. Definitely, kapag meron tayong (if we get a) source, then I will also would want to restore instead of putting it in the smaller projects that have no impact,” Ejercito said.

The Senate finance panel chairman previously questioned the reported realignment of around P206 billion in the House of Representatives' version of the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027.
Among the items he flagged was the P130-billion funding reduction for foreign-assisted projects.

He said the transportation sector also suffered a major cut of P40.4 billion, including P19.7 billion intended for the Metro Manila Subway Project and P15 billion for the North-South Commuter Railway. —LDF, GMA News
